claims.statement: Ruleset troubleshooting retains product/version availability from the pinned repo-rules reusable; frontmatter does not establish native eligibility or adoption.

Active rules can explain a blocked action. Signing or metadata restrictions may require rewriting, renaming, rebasing or squash merging; these are potential remedies requiring authorization, not commands run here or resolution of the earlier squash-metadata source contradiction.

Push rulesets allow at most 1,000 reference updates per push. Feature-gated file-path/file-size exceptions can be configured by eligible admins at repository, organization or enterprise scope; these source limits are not tested local behavior.
Push rulesets also apply to REST create-blob, create-tree and create/update-file-contents endpoints; UI-only testing does not cover all push surfaces.

Required names are job name, job name / reusable job name, or external check name. Workflow name, matrix and event types are not part of the required-status-check identity; identical names can therefore collide.
Above-repository check names are not indexed where enterprise rulesets are available, so names must be entered exactly. Evaluate runs checks without requiring them to pass.

Required workflows are organization/enterprise ruleset capabilities where gated. Creating a rule while a PR is already open does not automatically run it; a new commit, update or reopen can trigger it.

Required ruleset workflows support pull_request, pull_request_target and merge_group default activities; their supported-event filters are ignored. Events triggered by GITHUB_TOKEN do not run ruleset workflows.
Required workflows can block initialization of a new repository. Bootstrap before enforcing them, or use an explicitly authorized bypass; no bypass authority is inferred here.
The source recommends targeting PR integration branches rather than every branch, to avoid blocking ordinary development pushes.

Required workflows must be in .github/workflows. The source describes excluding the source repository or disabling Actions/a workflow for source-repository handling; these remain reference options and do not authorize disabling any estate capability.
Merge-queue required workflows need merge_group in their event list.

An external required workflow must be accessible within the organization. Its source visibility must be no more restrictive than targets: public can serve any target, internal can serve internal/private, and private can serve private.

Repository creation may require bypass when initial required workflows block it. Rule insights are logged only when a PR is merged or a merge is attempted; absence before an attempt is not a passing observation.

Do not use cancel-in-progress for workflows required by rulesets; cancellation can prevent satisfying the required workflow. This is scoped required-workflow guidance, not a ban on concurrency for all workflows.

scope: Full pinned article plus literal dependency reading; source evidence only, without adoption or live behavior verification.
